Welcome to PHYS 211, Fall 2026!

Not sure where to start? I've put together a guide.

This website contains the syllabus, schedule, FAQ, and links to useful resources to support your learning. If you are looking for handouts, in-class activities, specific assignments, or class slides, those will all be in the course page in Lyceum. If you are enrolled in the class but do not have access to Lyceum, please let me know immediately so I can add you.

# Get the textbook

If you have not yet, please make sure you get the textbook for this class, which is "Introduction to Classical Mechanics" by David Morin (Cambridge University Press). The library should have copies available, but you can also purchase it at the Bates bookstore.

![](images/Morin.jpg){width=200}

# Fill out the welcome form

The first thing you should do for this class is fill out the [welcome form](https://forms.gle/NUZQSNaDPxXRTite8). This form is quick and should be completed by the end of the first week of class. It will help me to support you in this class and will only take a few minutes of your time! This is also a chance for you to let me know your availability so I can optimize scheduling my office hours.

# Read the syllabus

I've tried to make the syllabus relatively short, sweet, and well-organized. It's all on this website, so please take a minute to read the [syllabus page](syllabus.qmd).

If you need help navigating to a specific topic in the syllabus, here's a rough outline:

[Classroom Expectations](syllabus.qmd#classexpectations)

[Technology and AI Policy](syllabus.qmd#techpolicy)

[Recording Policy](syllabus.qmd#recording)

[Grading Scheme](syllabus.qmd#grading)

[Assignments and Grading](syllabus.qmd#assignments)

[Deadline and Late Policy](syllabus.qmd#extensions)


# Keep an eye on the schedule

The schedule for this class is in a [google doc](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1YAsNtwv3fVJGBB0jJE1co742owqrAibKPeEpugopHsM/edit?usp=sharing) so that it can be updated as needed. Sometimes, things happen. Those things might be snow days, illnesses, travel, or just needing more time than anticipated on a topic. If needed, I may move due dates or adjust readings or topics in the schedule. I will talk about these changes in the classroom, but if you ever need to check a due date, the schedule will have the most up-to-date information.


# Need support?

Do you feel a little rusty with some of your math skills? Is there a topic you struggled with in previous physics classes and need to ask some questions? You can always come to office hours or schedule an appointment with me in calendly (see Lyceum for the link), but I've also put together a page with resources to support you.

On [this page](coursecontent.qmd), you will find a database of math videos if you need to brush up on some calculus you may have forgotten. You will also find a list of resources that might help if you're just having a tough time managing your workload, taking notes, or figuring out what to prioritize. 

There are also links on this page to mental health resources available on campus, including CAPS and the Title IX office.

# Still have questions?

If you've read the syllabus and still have questions, check out the [FAQ](FAQ.qmd). If you have a question that's not answered on that page, please feel free to email me! I've tried to collect the kinds of questions I get the most to save you time, but I know that not all questions can be answered with this website and am always happy to hear from you.

# Have concerns?

I know it can be intimidating to talk to a professor about sensitive topics. If something has made you uncomfortable, or if you think there is something I should know about, but don't feel comfortable speaking with me directly, I have an [anonymous feedback form](https://forms.gle/h1dzxVJKPEVo3v467) you can fill out. 

This form does not collect any identifying information (though you are welcome to leave your name if you want me to follow up with you). Please be respectful and thoughtful when filling out this form, as I use it to improve classroom dynamics and it's here to make everyone's experience better.
